[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Mastering Reusable Workflows and Composite Actions in GitHub Actions"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As CI/CD pipelines scale across organizations, maintaining DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principles becomes critical. GitHub Actions provides two powerful mechanisms for code reuse: Reusable Workflows and Composite Actions. Understanding when and how to use each will drastically improve your workflow efficiency and maintainability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Understanding the Core Differences"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Before diving into implementation, it is essential to understand the architectural differences between reusable workflows and composite actions."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Reusable Workflows allow you to run an entire workflow from another workflow. They run in their own isolated virtual environment and can contain multiple jobs."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Composite Actions allow you to bundle multiple workflow steps into a single action. They execute within the context of the calling job and share the same runner environment."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Building a Reusable Workflow"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Reusable workflows must be stored in the '.github/workflows' directory of a repository. They use the 'workflow_call' trigger to accept inputs and secrets from the caller workflow."},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"name: Reusable Build and Test

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      node-version:
        required: true
        type: string
    secrets:
      token:
        required: true

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node-version }}
      - name: Run Tests
        env:
          API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.token }}
        run: npm test"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Calling the Reusable Workflow"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"To invoke the reusable workflow defined above, use the 'uses' keyword within a job in another workflow file."},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"name: CI Pipeline

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  call-reusable:
    uses: owner/repo/.github/workflows/reusable.yml@main
    with:
      node-version: '18.x'
    secrets:
      token: ${{ secrets.CUSTOM_API_TOKEN }}"},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Creating a Composite Action"},{"order":14,"type":"paragraph","text":"Composite actions are defined using an 'action.yml' file placed in the root of an action repository or local directory. They are ideal for packaging repetitive sequences of steps, such as setting up a specific internal development environment."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"name: 'Setup Environment'
description: 'Installs dependencies and runs security checks'
inputs:
  env-name:
    description: 'Target environment'
    required: true
    default: 'development'
runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Dependencies
      run: npm install
      shell: bash
    - name: Run Security Audit
      run: npm audit --production
      shell: bash"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Using a Composite Action"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Once your composite action is defined, you can reference it inside any standard workflow step using the 'uses' keyword."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"name: Application Workflow

on: [push]

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Checkout Code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run Custom Setup
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-environment
        with:
          env-name: 'production'"},{"order":19,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices"},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Reusable Workflows for orchestrating entire deployment pipelines or multi-job workflows across repositories."},{"order":21,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Composite Actions for step-level logic, tool installations, and customized shell script wrappers."},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always pin reusable workflows and actions to a specific semantic version, commit SHA, or tag to ensure stability and security."}]
